quizName: DMV Practice Test #13 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When riding behind a car in the center of the lane:

options.text: The driver can see you in the rearview mirror.
The driver will have trouble seeing you.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver can see you in the rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: When following a car, ride where the driver can see you in their rearview mirror. This is usually the center of the lane. Drivers check their rearview mirrors often, so this position makes it more likely they will see you.

questions.question: You cannot get an intermediate permit if you are younger than:
questions.correctAnswerText: 16 years old.
questions.explanation: In Wyoming, you can get an instruction permit for a motorcycle at age 15. You can get an intermediate permit at age 16 if you have completed enough practice riding hours.

questions.question: What should you do when the lights on a railroad crossing sign are flashing?

options.text: Stop and wait until the train passes.
Turn around and take a different route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait until the train passes.
questions.explanation: At a railroad crossing with flashing lights, stop completely. Wait until the train passes and the lights stop flashing before you go. Never try to beat a train across the tracks.

questions.question: Helmets are:
questions.correctAnswerText: Required for all riders.
questions.explanation: Georgia law requires all riders to wear a U.S. Department of Transportation-compliant helmet every time they ride. A helmet is your best protection against head and neck injuries in a crash.

questions.question: A motorcyclist is usually most visible to other drivers when riding in which lane position?
questions.correctAnswerText: The center
questions.explanation: The center lane position is usually best when following a car because it puts you in the driver's rearview mirror. Always be ready to change positions based on traffic and conditions.

questions.question: Which is NOT a way to keep control of a motorcycle in a turn?
questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up through the turn.
questions.explanation: To stay in control during a turn, slow down before you enter it. Look through the turn where you want to go. Lean the motorcycle in the right direction and gently increase speed through the turn to keep the suspension stable.

questions.question: Motorcycles:

options.text: Stop in less distance than larger vehicles.
Need the same stopping distance as larger vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Need the same stopping distance as larger vehicles.
questions.explanation: Keep enough space between you and other vehicles for safe stopping. Motorcycles need as much stopping distance as other vehicles.

questions.question: When entering a curve, position your motorcycle:

options.text: On the outside of the curve.
On the inside of the curve.
Where you can safely handle the road and traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Where you can safely handle the road and traffic.
questions.explanation: Every curve is different. Choose a lane position that works for the conditions and adjust as needed.

questions.question: If a motorcycle is pulling a trailer, the following distance should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Increase.
questions.explanation: When towing a trailer, increase your following distance. The extra weight means your motorcycle needs more time to stop.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should:

options.text: Get closer to the vehicle ahead so you can see by its lights.
Keep your normal speed to avoid being hit from behind.
Slow down and increase your following distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and increase your following distance.
questions.explanation: When riding at night, go slower and stay farther back from other vehicles. It is harder to see at night, and you need extra time and space to react to dangers.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop completely. Then go when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely. Then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: Red octagonal signs are always stop signs. You must come to a complete stop, look for other traffic or pedestrians, and only go when it is safe.

questions.question: When driving on packed snow, how much should you reduce your speed?
questions.correctAnswerText: Half of your normal speed.
questions.explanation: On packed snow, reduce your speed to at least half of normal. Be extra careful on slippery surfaces.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: The front brake is stronger than the rear brake.
The rear brake is stronger than the front brake.
The front and rear brakes are equally strong.

questions.correctAnswerText: The front brake is stronger than the rear brake.
questions.explanation: The front brake is stronger than the rear brake. It provides at least 70 percent of the motorcycle's stopping power.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Merge.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that traffic will merge ahead.

questions.question: What does a solid white line on the side of the road mean?

options.text: The right edge of the traffic lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right edge of the traffic lane.
questions.explanation: A solid white line on the side of the road marks the right edge of the traffic lane.

questions.question: If your motorcycle weaves while crossing uneven metal bridge gratings, you should:

options.text: Downshift to a lower gear right away.
Ride in a zigzag pattern across the bridge.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay relaxed and steer straight.
questions.explanation: If your motorcycle weaves on uneven surfaces or bridge gratings, relax and go straight across at a steady speed. Zigzagging is more dangerous than the weaving.

questions.question: If you carry a load on your motorcycle, where should it go?

options.text: On the gas tank in front of you.
Piled against the back of the seat.

questions.correctAnswerText: Over the rear axle.
questions.explanation: Keep loads over or in front of the rear axle. Only experienced riders should carry loads.

questions.question: When reacting to a hazard, do NOT:

options.text: Let other drivers know you are there.
Use your horn, lights, or signals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let other drivers know you are there.
questions.explanation: Alert other drivers by using your horn, lights, and signals. Change your speed as needed. Move your lane position or direction to avoid the hazard.

questions.question: If your rear wheel locks while stopping on dry pavement, you should:

options.text: Keep the wheel locked until you stop.
Release the rear brake and use only the front brake.
Release and then quickly reapply the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the wheel locked until you stop.
questions.explanation: If the rear wheel locks on dry pavement, you can keep it locked until you stop. You can control the motorcycle if it stays upright and straight.

questions.question: How should you swerve correctly?

options.text: Press the handgrip toward the direction you want to turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handgrip toward the direction you want to turn.
questions.explanation: To swerve away from danger, press the handgrip on the side where you want to escape.

questions.question: Which is NOT a reason to keep space between your motorcycle and the vehicle in front of you?

options.text: It gives you more time to react to hazards.
It prevents you from finding an escape route.
It gives you space to move your motorcycle safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: It prevents you from finding an escape route.
questions.explanation: Space between you and the vehicle ahead gives you time to react if the other driver makes a mistake. It also gives you room to safely move your motorcycle.

questions.question: What is the maximum speed limit on the interstate if no other speed limit is posted?
questions.correctAnswerText: 80 mph
questions.explanation: The maximum speed limit on interstate highways in Wyoming is 75 or 80 mph. Always follow posted speed limits if they are different.

questions.question: When other vehicles are moving slowly or are stopped, what should a motorcyclist do?

options.text: A motorcyclist should not weave between lanes of traffic.
It is acceptable for a motorcyclist to weave in and out of traffic lanes.
A motorcyclist should ride in a straight line between two lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: A motorcyclist should not weave between lanes of traffic.
questions.explanation: Riding between rows of stopped or slow vehicles is dangerous. Other vehicles may change lanes, doors may open, or arms may stick out. Motorcycles need the full width of a lane to be safe.

questions.question: Smaller vehicles appear to be ________ and slower than they really are.
questions.correctAnswerText: Farther away
questions.explanation: It is hard to judge how fast a small vehicle is going or how far away it is. Do not assume that drivers of larger vehicles can judge your speed and location correctly.

questions.question: If you reach an intersection without traffic signals at the same time as another vehicle, what should happen?

options.text: The vehicle on the left should yield to the vehicle on the right.
You should flash your headlight to tell the other vehicle to go.
You should drive through and expect the other vehicle to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left should yield to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: At an intersection without signs or traffic lights, if two vehicles arrive at the same time, the vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
